label: prop:strangelet-double-beta
title: Strangelet interactions descend from the degree-2 fiber via double beta decay
html:
Proposition. Strangelet interactions descend from the degree-2 fiber via double beta decay

Let \mathcal{S} be a strangelet and \mathfrak{p} an ordinary hadron interacting with it. The interaction occurs in the degree-2 fiber of the chiral fibration, governed by the cinquefoil T_{2,5}^{\sigma} (5 crossings, genus 2). This sector is electromagnetically dark: the strangelet has Q = 0 (strangelet crossing energy), exchanging no photons.

Skein descent. Each crossing change in the Skein relation

  qL_+ - q^{-1}L_- = sL_0,
  \qquad s = q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2},

produces an L_0 smoothing. It splits into an electron (or positron) and a neutrino (beta decay products). The amplitude for each crossing change is s. Two crossing changes give the double beta amplitude s^2 and rate s^4:

  \Gamma_{2\beta} \sim s^4 \approx (0.104)^4 \sim 10^{-4}.

The interaction is suppressed by four powers of the Skein amplitude.

Observational signature. A strangelet passing through ordinary matter produces no electromagnetic ionization track. Its only interaction channel is double weak. It releases a pair of electrons (or positrons) and neutrinos. The interaction rate is exceptionally low, mimicking dark matter.
